label.en: Definition 5.1 — Angles, Transversals, and Polygon Theorems
label.ar: تعريف 5.1 — Angles, Transversals, and Polygon Theorems

body.en:
Fundamental properties of lines, intersecting angles, and polygons:
  • Angle Relationships: Complementary angles sum to \(90^\circ\); supplementary angles sum to \(180^\circ\); vertical opposite angles are strictly equal.
  • Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal: When two parallel lines \(L_1 \parallel L_2\) are intersected by a transversal, alternate interior, alternate exterior, and corresponding angles are equal; consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to \(180^\circ\)).
  • Polygon Angle Formulas: For any convex polygon with \(n\) sides:
    \[ \text{Sum of interior angles} = (n - 2) \cdot 180^\circ \]\[ \text{Each interior angle of a regular } n\text{-gon} = \frac{(n - 2) \cdot 180^\circ}{n} \]\[ \text{Sum of exterior angles} = 360^\circ \quad \left(\text{each regular exterior angle} = \frac{360^\circ}{n}\right) \]
body.ar:

body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: Theorem 5.1 — Right Triangles, Special Ratios, and Similarity Scaling
label.ar: مبرهنة 5.1 — Right Triangles, Special Ratios, and Similarity Scaling

body.en:
Right triangles and geometric similarity underpin top-tier ACT geometry problems:
  • Pythagorean Theorem: In any right triangle with legs \(a, b\) and hypotenuse \(c\), \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). Common integer triples include \(3-4-5\), \(5-12-13\), \(8-15-17\), \(7-24-25\), and their scale multiples (e.g., \(6-8-10\), \(9-12-15\)).
  • Special Right Triangles:
    \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) (Isosceles Right): Side ratio is \(x : x : x\sqrt{2}\).
    \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\): Side ratio opposite \(30^\circ : 60^\circ : 90^\circ\) is \(x : x\sqrt{3} : 2x\).
  • Similarity Scaling Law: If two similar figures have a linear scale ratio of \(k = \frac{s_2}{s_1}\):
    \[ \frac{\text{Perimeter}_2}{\text{Perimeter}_1} = k, \quad \frac{\text{Area}_2}{\text{Area}_1} = k^2, \quad \frac{\text{Volume}_2}{\text{Volume}_1} = k^3 \]
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: For any valid triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\):
    \[ |a - b| < c < a + b \]
body.ar:
Right triangles and geometric similarity underpin top-tier ACT الهندسة problems:
  • Pythagorean مبرهنة: In any right المثلث with legs \(a, b\) and hypotenuse \(c\), \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). Common integer triples include \(3-4-5\), \(5-12-13\), \(8-15-17\), \(7-24-25\), and their scale multiples (e.g., \(6-8-10\), \(9-12-15\)).
  • Special Right Triangles:
    \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) (Isosceles Right): Side ratio is \(x : x : x\sqrt{2}\).
    \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\): Side ratio opposite \(30^\circ : 60^\circ : 90^\circ\) is \(x : x\sqrt{3} : 2x\).
  • Similarity Scaling Law: If two similar figures have a linear scale ratio of \(k = \frac{s_2}{s_1}\):
    \[ \frac{\text{Perimeter}_2}{\text{Perimeter}_1} = k, \quad \frac{\text{Area}_2}{\text{Area}_1} = k^2, \quad \frac{\text{Volume}_2}{\text{Volume}_1} = k^3 \]
  • Triangle المتباينة مبرهنة: For any valid المثلث with side lengths \(a, b, c\):
    \[ |a - b| < c < a + b \]

body.en:
• Figures Are Not Necessarily to Scale: Unless explicitly noted, ACT figures are not drawn to scale. Never measure angles with your pencil or eye. Rely only on marked right angles, parallel indicators, or verified calculations.
  • Area Scaling with Dimension Changes: If the radius of a circle doubles, its area increases by \(2^2 = 4\) times, not 2 times! If all edges of a cube are tripled, its volume increases by \(3^3 = 27\) times.
  • Cylinder Surface Area vs. Lateral Area: Lateral area is \(2\pi r h\). Total surface area includes the top and bottom circles: \(2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h\). Watch whether the problem specifies an 'open top' or 'closed' cylinder.
  • Circumference vs. Arc Length: Arc length \(s = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}(2\pi r)\). Pay attention to whether the central angle is in degrees or radians (\(s = r\theta\) in radians).
body.ar:

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Plane Geometry)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Plane الهندسة)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

label.en: Worked Example 5.A — Special Right Triangle & Trapezoid Area
label.ar: مثال محلول 5.A — Special Right المثلث & Trapezoid المساحة

body.en:
In trapezoid \(ABCD\), bases \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) are parallel. Side \(\overline{AD}\) is perpendicular to both bases, with \(AD = 8\) and \(AB = 10\). If \(\angle BCD = 45^\circ\), what is the area of trapezoid \(ABCD\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Draw an altitude from vertex \(B\) perpendicular to \(\overline{CD}\) meeting at point \(E\). The height is \(BE = AD = 8\).
  2. Triangle \(BEC\) is a right triangle with right angle at \(E\). Since \(\angle BCD = 45^\circ\), \(\triangle BEC\) is a \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) special right triangle.
  3. Because legs are equal in a \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) triangle, \(EC = BE = 8\).
  4. Quadrilateral \(ABED\) is a rectangle, so \(DE = AB = 10\).
  5. The bottom base is \(CD = DE + EC = 10 + 8 = 18\).
  6. Compute the trapezoid area:
    \[ \text{Area} = \frac{b_1 + b_2}{2} \cdot h = \frac{10 + 18}{2} \cdot 8 = 14 \cdot 8 = 112 \]
The area of trapezoid \(ABCD\) is \(\mathbf{112}\) square units.
body.ar:
In trapezoid \(ABCD\), bases \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) are parallel. Side \(\overline{AD}\) is perpendicular to both bases, with \(AD = 8\) and \(AB = 10\). If \(\angle BCD = 45^\circ\), what is the المساحة of trapezoid \(ABCD\)?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Draw an altitude from الرأس \(B\) perpendicular to \(\overline{CD}\) meeting at point \(E\). The height is \(BE = AD = 8\).
  2. Triangle \(BEC\) is a right المثلث with right الزاوية at \(E\). Since \(\angle BCD = 45^\circ\), \(\triangle BEC\) is a \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) special right المثلث.
  3. Because legs are equal in a \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) المثلث, \(EC = BE = 8\).
  4. Quadrilateral \(ABED\) is a rectangle, so \(DE = AB = 10\).
  5. The bottom base is \(CD = DE + EC = 10 + 8 = 18\).
  6. Compute the trapezoid المساحة:
    \[ \text{Area} = \frac{b_1 + b_2}{2} \cdot h = \frac{10 + 18}{2} \cdot 8 = 14 \cdot 8 = 112 \]
The المساحة of trapezoid \(ABCD\) is \(\mathbf{112}\) square units.

label.en: Worked Example 5.B — Dimensional Scaling of 3D Prisms
label.ar: مثال محلول 5.B — Dimensional Scaling of 3D Prisms

body.en:
Solid Cylinder \(A\) has height \(6\) inches and radius \(4\) inches. Solid Cylinder \(B\) is geometrically similar to Cylinder \(A\) with a height of \(15\) inches. By what factor is the volume of Cylinder \(B\) larger than the volume of Cylinder \(A\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Find the linear scale factor \(k\):
    \[ k = \frac{h_B}{h_A} = \frac{15}{6} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5 \]
  2. Apply the volumetric scaling law for similar solids:
    \[ \frac{V_B}{V_A} = k^3 = \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{8} = 15.625 \]
  3. Verification via direct volume calculation:
    Radius of \(B\): \(r_B = 4 \cdot \frac{5}{2} = 10\).
    \(V_A = \pi(4^2)(6) = 96\pi\).
    \(V_B = \pi(10^2)(15) = 1500\pi\).
    Ratio: \(\frac{1500\pi}{96\pi} = \frac{125}{8} = 15.625\).
The volume of Cylinder \(B\) is \(\mathbf{\frac{125}{8}}\) (or \(\mathbf{15.625}\)) times that of Cylinder \(A\).
body.ar:
Solid Cylinder \(A\) has height \(6\) inches and نصف القطر \(4\) inches. Solid Cylinder \(B\) is geometrically similar to Cylinder \(A\) with a height of \(15\) inches. By what factor is the الحجم of Cylinder \(B\) larger than the الحجم of Cylinder \(A\)?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Find the linear scale factor \(k\):
    \[ k = \frac{h_B}{h_A} = \frac{15}{6} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5 \]
  2. Apply the volumetric scaling law for similar solids:
    \[ \frac{V_B}{V_A} = k^3 = \left(\frac{5}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{8} = 15.625 \]
  3. Verification via direct الحجم calculation:
    Radius of \(B\): \(r_B = 4 \cdot \frac{5}{2} = 10\).
    \(V_A = \pi(4^2)(6) = 96\pi\).
    \(V_B = \pi(10^2)(15) = 1500\pi\).
    Ratio: \(\frac{1500\pi}{96\pi} = \frac{125}{8} = 15.625\).
The الحجم of Cylinder \(B\) is \(\mathbf{\frac{125}{8}}\) (or \(\mathbf{15.625}\)) times that of Cylinder \(A\).

label.en: Worked Example 5.C — Inscribed vs Central Angles in a Circle
label.ar: مثال محلول 5.C — Inscribed vs Central Angles in a الدائرة

body.en:
Points \(A, B, C\) lie on a circle centered at \(O\). If central angle \(\angle AOB = 114^\circ\), what is the measure of inscribed angle \(\angle ACB\) subtending the same minor arc \(\widehat{AB}\)?

Solution: By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, an inscribed angle equals half the central angle subtending the same arc:
\[ \angle ACB = \frac{1}{2}(114^\circ) = \mathbf{57^\circ} \]
body.ar:
Points \(A, B, C\) lie on a الدائرة centered at \(O\). If central الزاوية \(\angle AOB = 114^\circ\), what is the measure of inscribed الزاوية \(\angle ACB\) subtending the same minor arc \(\widehat{AB}\)?

Solution: By the Inscribed الزاوية مبرهنة, an inscribed الزاوية equals half the central الزاوية subtending the same arc:
\[ \angle ACB = \frac{1}{2}(114^\circ) = \mathbf{57^\circ} \]

label.en: Worked Example 5.D — Space Diagonal of a 3D Rectangular Prism
label.ar: مثال محلول 5.D — Space Diagonal of a 3D Rectangular Prism

body.en:
Find the length of the longest rod that can fit completely inside a rectangular box of dimensions \(3\text{ ft} \times 4\text{ ft} \times 12\text{ ft}\).

Solution: Apply the 3D Pythagorean theorem:
\[ d = \sqrt{\ell^2 + w^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = \mathbf{13\text{ ft}} \]

question.en: A right circular cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. What is its total surface area in terms of \(\pi\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Plane Geometry): A right circular cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. What is its total surface area in terms of \(\pi\)?

solution.en:
The total surface area includes the two circular bases and the lateral curved surface:
\[ \text{TSA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(8) = 18\pi + 48\pi = \mathbf{66\pi} \text{ cm}^2 \]
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: The total surface area includes the two circular bases and the lateral curved surface:
\[ \text{TSA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(8) = 18\pi + 48\pi = \mathbf{66\pi} \text{ cm}^2 \]

question.en: Two sides of a non-degenerate triangle measure 7 inches and 11 inches. What is the range of possible perimeters for this triangle?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Plane Geometry): Two sides of a non-degenerate triangle measure 7 inches and 11 inches. What is the range of possible perimeters for this triangle?

solution.en:
Let \(x\) be the third side. By the Triangle Inequality Theorem, \(11 - 7 < x < 11 + 7 \implies 4 < x < 18\).
The perimeter is \(P = 7 + 11 + x = 18 + x\).
Substituting the strict bounds for \(x\):
\[ 18 + 4 < P < 18 + 18 \implies \mathbf{22 < P < 36} \text{ inches} \]

\[ 18 + 4 < P < 18 + 18 \implies \mathbf{22 < P < 36} \text{ inches} \]

question.en: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures \(150^\circ\). How many sides does this polygon have?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Plane Geometry): Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures \(150^\circ\). How many sides does this polygon have?

solution.en:
Using the exterior angle method (much faster on the ACT than interior angles):
Each exterior angle is supplementary to the interior angle: \(180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ\).
Since the exterior angles of any regular polygon sum to \(360^\circ\):
\[ n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = \mathbf{12} \text{ sides (dodecagon)} \]
solution.ar:

Each exterior angle is supplementary to the interior angle: \(180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ\).
Since the exterior angles of any regular polygon sum to \(360^\circ\):
\[ n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = \mathbf{12} \text{ sides (dodecagon)} \]

question.en: A circle has a radius of 12 cm. What is the area of a sector formed by a central angle of \(75^\circ\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Plane Geometry): A circle has a radius of 12 cm. What is the area of a sector formed by a central angle of \(75^\circ\)?

solution.en:
The formula for the area of a circle sector is:
\[ A = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \pi r^2 = \frac{75}{360} \pi (12^2) = \frac{5}{24} \cdot 144\pi = 5 \cdot 6\pi = \mathbf{30\pi} \text{ cm}^2 \]

question.en: An isosceles trapezoid has parallel bases of lengths 4 cm and 16 cm. A circle is inscribed inside the trapezoid such that it is tangent to all four sides. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the region inside the trapezoid that lies outside the circle?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Plane Geometry): An isosceles trapezoid has parallel bases of lengths 4 cm and 16 cm. A circle is inscribed inside the trapezoid such that it is tangent to all four sides. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the region inside the trapezoid that lies outside the circle?

hints.en: Determine the leg lengths of the trapezoid: Let the trapezoid be \(ABCD\) with parallel bases \(AB = 4\) cm and \(CD = 16\) cm, and nonparallel legs \(AD = BC\).
hints.ar: حدّد leg lengths of the trapezoid: ليكن the trapezoid be \(ABCD\) with parallel bases \(AB = 4\) cm and \(CD = 16\) cm, and nonparallel legs \(AD = BC\).

hints.en: By the Pythagorean theorem on the resulting right triangle: \(h^2 + 6^2 = 10^2 \implies h^2 + 36 = 100 \implies h^2 = 64 \implies h\).
hints.ar: بتطبيق Pythagorean theorem on the resulting right triangle: \(h^2 + 6^2 = 10^2 \implies h^2 + 36 = 100 \implies h^2 = 64 \implies h\).

hints.en: - Area of the region outside the circle: \(\text{Area} = 80 - 16\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\text{Area} = 80 - 16\pi\text{ cm}^2\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
1. **Determine the leg lengths of the trapezoid:**
Let the trapezoid be \(ABCD\) with parallel bases \(AB = 4\) cm and \(CD = 16\) cm, and nonparallel legs \(AD = BC\).
Because a circle is tangent to all four sides, the trapezoid is a tangential quadrilateral. Tangent segments drawn from any vertex to the circle are equal in length. By symmetry, the points of tangency on the bases bisect each base:
- The segments from the top vertices to the top tangency point each measure \(4 / 2 = 2\) cm.
- The segments from the bottom vertices to the bottom tangency point each measure \(16 / 2 = 8\) cm.

Therefore, each leg has length:
\[
AD = BC = 2 + 8 = 10\text{ cm}
\]

2. **Find the height of the trapezoid:**
Drop perpendicular altitudes from the endpoints of the shorter base to the longer base. The projection of each slanted leg onto the longer base has length:
\[
\frac{16 - 4}{2} = 6\text{ cm}
\]
By the Pythagorean theorem on the resulting right triangle:
\[
h^2 + 6^2 = 10^2 \implies h^2 + 36 = 100 \implies h^2 = 64 \implies h = 8\text{ cm}
\]

3. **Calculate the radius of the inscribed circle:**
The distance between the horizontal parallel tangent lines is the diameter of the circle, so:
\[
2r = h = 8\text{ cm} \implies r = 4\text{ cm}
\]

4. **Calculate the required area:**
- Area of the trapezoid:
\[
\text{Area}_{\text{trap}} = \frac{4 + 16}{2} \times 8 = 10 \times 8 = 80\text{ cm}^2
\]
- Area of the inscribed circle:
\[
\text{Area}_{\text{circle}} = \pi r^2 = \pi (4^2) = 16\pi\text{ cm}^2
\]
- Area of the region outside the circle:
\[
\text{Area} = 80 - 16\pi\text{ cm}^2
\]

Common Misconceptions:
- Misconception 1 (Choice B): Assuming the circle's diameter is the average of the bases (\(10\)), which would incorrectly give \(r = 5\) and an area of \(80 - 25\pi\).
- Misconception 2 (Choice C): Conflating the leg length with the perpendicular height (\(h = 10\)), yielding a trapezoid area of \(100\) and circle area of \(25\pi\).
